newsitem.title: USA: NY precious metals soar on short covering rally.
newsitem.headline: NY precious metals soar on short covering rally.

text.p: New York precious metals futures ended sharply higher Wednesday, as trade buying and fund short covering rescued gold from a new three year low seen early and end up benefitting the whole complex.
"Why today? Well why not?" Credit Lyonnais Rouse New York chief bullion dealer Scott Mehlman said.
"There was no news, but the market has been very short for some time, and we broke up through some downtrend levels today which triggered heavy fund buying", he said.
COMEX April gold ended up $3.50 an ounce at $345.40, after seeing a five day high intraday at $348.00.
Total estimated COMEX gold volume was 70,000 lots.

Earlier, new contract lows had been seen in all COMEX gold delivery months out to December 1997, as the US dollar continued its rally to 34 month highs against the mark, and ongoing declines in gold prices in Australian dollars and South African rand renewed concern about producer hedging.

In the bullion market, spot gold ended quoted $342.80/30, compared to the London Wednesday afternoon fix at $337.70 and the Wednesday morning fix at $336.90 which was the lowest level since April 13, 1993. In New York Wednesday spot gold closed around $339.80/30.

Commodity funds have been running near record short positions in gold in recent months, as talk of European central bank sales, and disinvestment from hard assets in the face of soaring US equity markets, drove gold prices lower.

COMEX open interest in gold futures has also been running close to 200,000 lots, a level which also proved unsustainable in February last year, when gold prices reached five year highs, analysts noted.
"There must surely come a point when short sales are reversed," Gold Fields Mineral Services analyst Stewart Murray said in a recent report.
"If this happens in the near future and, in the absence of increased supply from the official sector or producer hedging, then the market could once again see a robust rally.
COMEX March silver ended up 29.7 cents an ounce at $5.135, after seeing a five month intraday high at $5.220. Total estimated COMEX silver volume was a high 65,000 contracts.
Silver, with less bearish fundamentals than gold, had been recovering from a year-long downtrend since early January, helped by some heavy investment fund buying, analysts said.
When support around $4.80 an ounce in COMEX March silver held again Wednesday, fresh buying emerged, driving prices sharply higher, traders said.
The spot gold/silver ratio continued to favor silver also, falling to a new 16 month low at 66.80.
The widening differential between gold and the platinum metals group also sparked some buying of gold, traders said.
Palladium prices are now at their highest levels since May 1996, while platinum prices are at four week highs.

NYMEX April platinum ended up $13.00 an ounce at $371.50, with the April COMEX gold/NYMEX platinum spread soaring to end at contract highs at $26.50 an ounce, up from $16.90 Tuesday, and $11.90 at the end of last week.

"There was heavy trade buying and short covering in platinum, despite the news the Russian parliament passed the 1997 budget which should ease some of the platinum and palladium supply problems," Refco New York analyst Jim Steel said.
COMEX March palladium ended up $3.90 an ounce at $140.50, a contract high also.

Concern about Russian platinum and palladium supplies, due to Russian fiscal problems, a breakdown in Russian/Japanese palladium contract talks and rumors of a rundown in Russian stocks, had helped palladium to recover steadily in recent weeks.
